limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings between 50,210 and 144,380: 88% of the 225 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (218 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 17,160 against 37,081; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.

Candidates ['prior_earnings', 'distance_km'] passed the joint-test rule, but the R-learner smooth on them does not beat a constant effect by more than one SE (gain 914,901, SE 2,187,143); none is claimed.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: prior_earnings p=0.0188 (+5482, +6149, +4466, +9160 dollars per SD); distance_km p=0.0492 (-1687, -1346, -1656, -1215 dollars per SD); education p=0.821 (+292, +437, -48, +286 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
14.2% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 6,251 dollars.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 30,972.0 (train) against 25,196.5 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 8.3%. 327 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 13,720 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 5.9%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['prior_earnings', 'distance_km', 'education'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
